prose_changes.old: William Booth gave up his Methodist pulpit in 1861 to preach in the streets of London's East End, and by 1878 his Christian Mission had renamed itself an Army, with ranks, uniforms, and brass bands to drown out hecklers. Catherine Booth had already argued, in 1859, that women should be commissioned as officers on equal terms with men, and the Army counted everything it did, soul by soul and meal by meal, in the scheme for shelters and labor it published as In Darkest England in 1890.
prose_changes.new: William Booth gave up his Methodist pulpit in 1861, and by 1865 he was preaching in the streets of London's East End. By 1878 his Christian Mission had renamed itself an Army, with ranks, uniforms, and brass bands to drown out hecklers. Catherine Booth had already argued in print, in 1859, that women had the right to preach, and the Army commissioned women as officers from the start. It counted everything it did, soul by soul and meal by meal. In 1890 it published its scheme for shelters and labor as In Darkest England.
prose_changes.reason: 'In 1859 ... women should be commissioned as officers' is anachronistic: there was no Army and no officers until 1878. Her 1859 pamphlet (Female Ministry) argued women's right to preach; the Army's commissioning of women officers from the start is the entry's own source note. The 1861/1865 dates are split as the description has them. Sentences shortened; every other fact kept.

prose_changes.old: Anglo-Catholicism became a permanent party inside Anglicanism and is still there, worldwide — its ceremonial, its parish schools and its slum priests changed what an ordinary English church service looks and sounds like, and the religious orders it revived are still in existence. Its hymn-writers and translators put a great deal of ancient and medieval material into English hymnals used far outside its own circles, and its recovery of early liturgy fed into the twentieth-century liturgical reforms of churches that had no sympathy with its politics at all. Newman went the other way and became a cardinal; he was canonized by the Roman Catholic Church in 2019.
prose_changes.new: Anglo-Catholicism became a lasting party inside Anglicanism, and it is still there, worldwide. Its ritual, its parish schools and its slum priests changed how an ordinary English church service looks and sounds. The religious orders it revived still exist. Its hymn-writers and translators put a great deal of ancient and medieval writing into English hymn books. Many people far outside its circles sing from them. Its scholars also put the early forms of Eastern worship into English. Newman went the other way and became a cardinal. The Roman Catholic Church made him a saint in 2019.
prose_changes.reason: Removed the unsupported claim that its recovery of early liturgy 'fed into the twentieth-century liturgical reforms of churches that had no sympathy with its politics'. Kept what a vendored text shows: Neale and Littledale's English translations of the early Eastern liturgies. Other facts kept; long sentences split for reading level.
